[[File:ClusterBomb-NEGWT.png|thumb|right|250px|An anti-starfighter cluster bomb.]]
A '''cluster bomb''', also known as a '''cluster trap''', was an explosive device, often disguised to blend in the with the [[Hull/Legends|hull]] of the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] it was mounted on. The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] made use of concealed cluster bombs aboard their ships.

==Description==
A cluster bomb was a metal blister that was mounted to the [[Hull/Legends|hull]] of a [[Starship/Legends|starship]], designed to blend in with the vessel's superstructure.<ref name="EGWT">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> The weapon was intended to target and destroy small enemy [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] formations during combat by catching them unawares within an explosive blast. Relying on the element of surprise, cluster bombs were deadly at close range,<ref name="NEGWT">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> and were most effective against closely-packed enemy ships allowing them to destroy multiple vessels at a time. As such, they were often successfully deployed in [[Space warfare/Legends|battles]] where enemy fighters vastly outnumbered friendly ships.<ref name="EGWT" />

When detonated, the blister's shell was reduced to shrapnel.<ref name="NEGWT" /> [[Explosive charge/Legends|explosive charges]] propelled the shrapnel and dozens of [[Magnet/Legends|magnetized]] [[Proton grenade/Legends|proton]] and [[Concussion grenade/Legends|concussion grenades]] out into [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. The cloud of explosives and debris spread over an area of one hundred [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in diameter. The magnetized [[Grenade/Legends|grenades]] homed in on any ships in the area, creating chain reactions of explosions that turned the immediate area into a hazard zone.<ref name="EGWT" />

[[Explosive dampener]]s protected the ship during the cluster bomb's detonation,<ref name="EGWT" /> ensuring that the [[Warship/Legends|warships]] themselves were not damaged by the initial explosions.<ref name="NEGWT" /> The grenades were not powerful enough to pierce the [[Armor/Legends|armor]] plating of a [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]]. The dampeners had breakaway panels that allowed fresh cluster bombs to be replaced by maintenance crews in less than ten [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]].<ref name="EGWT" />

Cluster bombs were activated by the [[Gunner/Legends|gunnery]] crews aboard a ship; the module's short-range sensors swept for enemy [[Transponder code/Legends|transponder codes]] in the bomb's vicinity. Depending on the programming used in the bomb, the weapon would detonate once it detected between one and six ships in its blast radius. The cluster bombs were monitored by the gunnery crews who could initiate an emergency override to prevent detonation in case friendly fighters were in the blast range.<ref name="EGWT" />

Cluster bombs were mounted onto the outer hulls of starships, including [[Mon Calamari Star Cruiser/Legends|Mon Calamari Star Cruisers]] and [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigates]].<ref name="EGWT" /> Cluster Bombs were housed in angular casings that resemble cargo modules<ref name="NEGWT" />, though on [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] vessels the bombs were disguised to appear identical to the ovoid shapes that were commonly placed across the hull. The ovoids usually held weapons emplacements, sensor array blisters, and cargo modules.<ref name="NEGWT" /> More traditionally designed ships had cluster bombs designed to look like [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] clusters or cargo [[Airlock/Legends|airlocks]].<ref name="EGWT" />

Some cluster bombs included [[false signal generator]]s that produced emissions masking the device's true nature and gave the enemy the impression that they were active [[Sensor array/Legends|sensor arrays]]. Enemy [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] were lured in to attack a seemingly vital target, only to be destroyed by an active cluster bomb.<ref name="EGWT" />

[[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] ships broadcasted warnings to friendly vessels about the cluster bombs, and [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] in an engagement zone often memorized the locations of the cluster bombs so they would not fly into their blast radius.<ref name="EGWT" />

During the early [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the New Republic, [[FreiTek Incorporated/Legends|FreiTek Incorporated]] manufactured the [[CL-3 antistarfighter cluster bomb]].<ref name="EGWT" />

==History==
When the Mon Calamari began arming their star [[Cruiser/Legends|cruisers]] after joining the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]] authorized the integration of cluster bombs into the ships.<ref name="NEGWT" />

During the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], [[Rebel pilot/Legends|Rebel pilots]] memorized the location of cluster bombs on the hulls of the Mon Calamari cruisers, making sure to avoid the blisters during the engagement. [[Squadron/Legends|Squadrons]] of [[TIE pilot]]s were destroyed in cluster bomb explosions as they rushed headlong into battle, following their training to be aggressive and overzealous in combat while attacking in large formations.<ref name="NEGWT" />

The [[Inquisition module]] of [[Tagge Industries Shipyards Limited]]'s [[modular taskforce cruiser]] carried five cluster bombs armed with [[magnepulse bomb]]s.<ref name="DESB">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref>
